# Jubilees Chapter 44 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob's last blessings; the tribal prophecies; bury me at Machpelah

---

**44:1** In the forty-fifth jubilee, fifth week, first year, Joseph brought his two sons to visit their grandfather Jacob.

**44:2** Jacob looked at the boys. "Who are these?" — "My sons, Father. God gave them to me here in Egypt." — "Bring them to me. I want to bless them."

**44:3** Jacob blessed the boys — but he crossed his arms. Ephraim on his right, Manasseh on his left, even though Manasseh was the elder.

**44:4** Joseph tried to correct him: "Father — Manasseh's the firstborn. Right hand on him." Jacob wouldn't move his hands. "I know, son. I know. Manasseh will be great too. But Ephraim will be greater. His descendants will fill the nations."

**44:5** Jacob pronounced the blessing that would become the standard in Israel: "May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh." Ephraim first.

**44:6** Then Jacob summoned all his sons: "Come close — I'll tell you what's coming for each of you."

**44:7** He went through them one by one.

**44:8** To Reuben he said: "My firstborn — my strength, the prime of my power. You should have had the highest honor. But you're unstable as water, and you'll never rise to the top. You climbed into my bed, Reuben. You violated it."

**44:9** Of Simeon and Levi together: "Brothers in blood — partners in brutality. I want nothing to do with the plans they make or the gangs they run. They killed men out of anger. They mutilated animals out of spite. Cursed is that rage. I am splitting them up — Simeon and Levi divided across the land of Israel."

**44:10** To Judah: "Your brothers will bow to you, Judah. Your hand will grip the throats of your enemies. You are a young lion. The scepter stays with Judah — the royal staff between his feet — until the one it truly belongs to comes, and the nations obey him."

**44:11** He blessed each son in turn with what was fitting for him. And he gave them his final charge: "When I die, bury me at Machpelah — Ephron the Hittite's field."

---

*PNEUMA notes: The crossing of hands for Ephraim over Manasseh (v.3) is preserved faithfully. The tribal blessings quote Reuben, Simeon/Levi, and Judah from Genesis 49. The repetition of the scepter oracle (v.10 = ch.38:14) reinforces Judah's royal destiny as a recurring theme in Jubilees' final chapters.*
